简单取放.recommendation: The two-step simple pick-and-place decomposition (skill_005) is consistently used and successful across all 24 episodes; keep it as the default plan for this task family.

Several successful episodes spent many steps opening closed drawers/cabinets before finding the target on an open surface (e.g., episode_007 found candle on toilet after scanning many closed cabinets; episode_017 found keychain on sidetable after opening many drawers). Reinforce skill_002: prioritize open surfaces before closed containers to reduce wasted steps.

When the target is not on the first open surface, the successful plans systematically moved to new unchecked plausible locations (e.g., episode_011 scanned cabinets then found pan on countertop; episode_015 found soapbottle on diningtable after many locations). Keep the systematic candidate-location tracking from skill_003.

For placement into closed containers (cabinet/drawer), the successful plan opened the container before putting (episode_023 opened cabinet 1 then put soapbottle). Include an explicit open step when the destination is a closed container.

Search efficiency varies widely: some episodes took 30+ steps (episode_017, episode_015) while similar goals succeeded in 4-5 steps. Consider prioritizing high-probability open surfaces (sidetable, desk, dresser, countertop) before exhaustive closed-container sweeps to bound search length.

台灯观察.recommendation: Initial plans should decompose 台灯观察 as: locate and turn on the desklamp first (or locate target then bring it to the desklamp), then take the target object, then perform examine/look. Avoid planning to take the desklamp itself, since take desklamp fails and the lamp must stay in place as the light source.

When the target object is not on an open surface, systematically search closed containers (drawers/cabinets) by opening them one by one, and mark each checked location before moving on. Do not loop over the same drawers or wander without a candidate list.

After turning on the desklamp and having the target object co-located, the plan must include an explicit examine/look action; merely putting the object on the desk or lamp does not satisfy the observation goal.

Prefer checking open surfaces (desk, dresser, sidetable, bed, shelf, coffeetable) for both the target object and the desklamp before opening closed containers; most successful episodes found both on open surfaces in the first few steps.

After a take or use action, verify the observation before proceeding; failed take attempts (e.g., 'Nothing happens') should trigger a retry with the correct object id or a move to a new location rather than continuing blindly.

清洗后放置.recommendation: The three-step clean-then-place decomposition (take, clean at sinkbasin, put at destination) is consistently used and succeeds across most episodes; keep it as the default plan for this task family.

When the target object is not on open surfaces, search closed containers systematically but bound the search; episode_069 exhausted many drawers/cabinets without finding a knife and failed, and episode_044/056/063/070 spent many steps opening cabinets before locating the item. Prioritize high-probability locations and avoid unbounded cabinet sweeps.

Some objects (towel/cloth) do not support clean at sinkbasin; episode_049 repeatedly attempted clean on a towel with no effect and failed. When the goal names a cloth-like item, verify cleanability or substitute a cleanable object rather than retrying the same clean action.

When clean fails on the first attempt, retry after repositioning or re-approaching the sinkbasin rather than repeating identical clean calls; episode_061 succeeded only after putting the lettuce on the sinkbasin and re-taking it, while episode_071 succeeded on a second clean after moving to the sinkbasin.

Verify the destination container is open and usable before placing; episode_059 failed because put into coffeemachine did nothing and open coffeemachine also did nothing. Check container state and consider alternatives if the target is not placeable.

Match the object type to the goal noun: episode_052 used a butterknife for a 'knife' goal and episode_060 used a mug for a 'cup' goal, both ending without environment win. Prefer the exact object class named in the goal when available.

Episode_053 substituted a pan for a pot goal and placed it on the stoveburner, completing without environment win. When the named object is unavailable, do not silently substitute a different object class; continue searching or report the mismatch.

After each critical action (take, clean, put), confirm success from the observation before proceeding; several failures stemmed from continuing after a no-op action (episode_049, episode_059, episode_052).

加热后放置.recommendation: The initial plan should explicitly include opening the microwave before placing the object and closing it before heating, and should verify the object is hot before taking it. Several successful episodes (074, 085, 091) show the object must be inside an open microwave; episode 088 failed because heat was attempted while the microwave was closed, and episode 090 failed because the egg was never successfully heated before placement.

When the target object is not found in the first few likely locations, avoid an unbounded search across many cabinets/drawers. Episodes 078, 093, and 096 exhausted steps searching dozens of closed containers and failed; limit search to high-probability locations and reconsider the plan.

After a heat action, confirm the object is actually hot before taking and placing it. In episode 090 the egg was never heated yet the plan proceeded to place it, and in episode 089 the egg was never successfully heated before repeated failed put attempts.
After each put action, check the observation to confirm placement succeeded. Episodes 089 and 090 show repeated 'Nothing happens' put attempts that were not corrected, leading to plan failure.

For heat-then-place goals, take the heated object directly to the final destination without inserting intermediate placements. Episode 077 and 080 show the object was placed in the microwave, taken, heated, then moved directly to the destination, which succeeded.

When the goal names a specific object type (e.g., mug, cup, plate), ensure the taken object matches that type. Episode 081 took a mug for a 'cup' goal and episode 088 took a cup for a 'mug' goal; both ended without environment win, suggesting object-type mismatch can prevent goal satisfaction.

Locate the target object by checking open surfaces first before opening many closed containers. Episodes 074, 077, 084, and 087 found the target on an open countertop quickly, while episodes 078 and 096 wasted many steps opening closed cabinets.

Before placing into a destination container, ensure it is open and has space. Episodes 077, 080, and 091 opened the cabinet/fridge before putting, which succeeded; episode 090 attempted puts into a closed fridge repeatedly with no effect.

冷却后放置.recommendation: The cooling step is being executed as put-in-fridge then immediately take-out, which does not actually cool the object; many episodes end plan_completed_without_environment_win after this pattern. The plan should treat cooling as a state change requiring verification (e.g., confirm the object is cool before retrieval), not just a round-trip through the fridge.

Several episodes take an object that was already inside the fridge and skip any explicit cooling action, then place it at the destination and fail. Even when the object is found in the fridge, the plan should include an explicit cool/verify step rather than assuming the initial location satisfies the cooled state.

Episodes 097, 100, 114, and 115 fail with plan_failed after long searches across many cabinets/drawers for the target object (bowl, potato, pan, egg). The plan should limit search to a few high-probability locations and, if not found, revise the plan or consider an alternative object rather than looping through every container.

In episode 098 the plan placed the pot into cabinet 5 without ever performing the cooling step, and the episode ended plan_completed_without_environment_win. The initial plan must include the explicit fridge cooling sub-step before the final placement, not just a search for an empty cabinet.

Episode 102's goal was a cool cup but the plan took a mug instead, and episode 108/109 similarly used a mug for a cup goal. The plan should match the exact target object type (cup vs mug) before proceeding, since substituting a different object type can fail the goal.

Several episodes show the agent attempting put/take actions before navigating to the fridge (e.g., 'put mug in/on fridge 1' returning 'Nothing happens', then later going to fridge). The plan should order navigation to the appliance before the put/take action, and verify success before continuing.

Episode 116 shows the agent taking the winebottle from the countertop, then later taking it again from the fridge, indicating the object was placed in the fridge without an explicit cooling action and the plan lost track of state. The plan should keep explicit track of where the object is and whether it has been cooled.

双物品放置.recommendation: The sequential two-item plan (skill_022) is sound and should be kept, but add an explicit verification step after each put: check the observation to confirm the item is actually on/in the target before searching for the second item. In episode_132 the first newspaper was taken but never confirmed placed on armchair 1, and the plan ended with only newspaper 2 on the armchair.

When the first put fails or is skipped, do not proceed to the second item. In episode_133 creditcard 2 was taken and the agent went to armchair 1 but no put succeeded; it then searched for creditcard 1 and ended with creditcard 2 still on the armchair and creditcard 1 never placed. Retry the failed put at the target before continuing.

For soapbottle searches, prioritize open surfaces and visible locations (toilet, countertop, bathtubbasin, garbagecan) before opening many closed cabinets. In episode_118 the agent opened cabinet 1 and found soapbottle 2, but then wandered through cabinets 2-5 and garbagecan before finally finding soapbottle 2 on toilet 1; in episode_121 it searched shelves and basins and never found a second soapbottle, failing.

Maintain a checked-location list and avoid revisiting the same empty surfaces repeatedly. In episode_121 the agent cycled through sinkbasin 1, shelves, countertop and back to sinkbasin 1 multiple times without finding the second soapbottle; mark each location checked and move to new plausible spots.

When the target container is closed, open it before placing, and confirm the put succeeded. In episode_128 the agent opened cabinet 1 then placed peppershaker 1, and in episode_130 opened cabinet 1 before placing saltshakers; keep this open-then-put ordering explicit in the plan for closed destinations.

Prefer searching open surfaces first for common household items: remotecontrol/watch/creditcard on coffeetable, diningtable, sofa; pen on diningtable; cloth on dresser/countertop; pillow on sofa; handtowel on handtowelholder. Successful episodes found both items quickly this way, while failures spent many steps on closed drawers and cabinets.

When a put action returns 'Nothing happens', navigate to the target location and retry the put rather than continuing the search. In episode_129 a put of creditcard 3 on sofa 1 returned 'Nothing happens' at step 8; the agent later went to sofa 1 and successfully placed it at step 10, showing the retry pattern works.

Limit exhaustive closed-container sweeps when the second item is likely on an open surface. In episode_134 the agent opened drawers 1-4 and cabinets 1-4 before returning to countertop 1 to find spoon 2; checking countertop 1 again earlier would have saved many steps.

简单取放.recommendation: When the target object is not visible, search open surfaces (sidetables, dressers, beds, sofas, desks, countertops) before opening closed containers; this consistently located objects quickly across episodes.
Avoid navigating to a drawer as a standalone location; 'go to drawer N' often returns 'Nothing happens'. Navigate to the parent furniture or open the drawer directly when already at it.
Open closed containers before checking or placing inside them; opening cabinets/drawers revealed contents and enabled successful placement.
Follow the consistent take-then-navigate-then-put sequence: after taking the object, go to the destination receptacle, then put the object there. This pattern succeeded in nearly every episode.
Do not attempt 'open' on non-container surfaces like desks or tables; only open closed containers such as drawers, cabinets, fridges, and microwaves.
When a likely location is empty, move on promptly to the next plausible receptacle rather than retrying the same spot; this kept searches efficient and within budget.

台灯观察.recommendation: When the target object is already visible on a surface near the desklamp, take it first, then navigate to the desklamp's surface and use the desklamp. Avoid wandering to unrelated receptacles after the object is in hand.
Do not attempt to take the desklamp; it is fixed. When holding the target object and standing at the desklamp's surface, issue use desklamp directly instead of trying to pick up the lamp.

After arriving at the desklamp's surface, do not repeat go to the same desk or attempt go to loc <id>; these return Nothing happens. Use the desklamp or look/examine the surface to confirm contents instead.

Search open surfaces (desks, dressers, sidetables, beds, coffeetables) before opening drawers; in these tasks the target object and desklamp were almost always on open surfaces, and drawer sweeps wasted steps.

When the desklamp is not on the first desk checked, continue to other likely surfaces (dresser, sidetable, shelf) rather than retrying the same desk; the lamp may be on a different surface than the target object.
Use exact object identifiers when taking (e.g., take alarmclock 1 from desk 1); bare names like take alarmclock can return Nothing happens even when the object is present.
Avoid examine on non-container surfaces and avoid open on drawers that are not openable in the current room; these produce Nothing happens. Prefer look or go to the surface to observe contents.

In episode 033 the plan failed after taking the statue and then searching many drawers for a desklamp that was already visible on sidetable 1. When the desklamp is already observed, go directly to its surface and use it rather than continuing to search.

清洗后放置.recommendation: When a clean-and-place task names a generic object (e.g., 'pot', 'knife', 'cup'), accept a close synonym found in the environment (pan for pot, butterknife for knife, mug for cup) and proceed with clean+place rather than continuing to search for the exact name; several successes did this, while exhaustive cabinet/drawer sweeps for the literal name failed.

Do not attempt to clean a towel/cloth with a sinkbasin; the clean action returns 'Nothing happens' repeatedly. If the target is a towel, treat it as non-cleanable and avoid burning steps on clean/use/examine retries.

Do not assume a coffeemachine accepts a placed mug/cup; put and open both returned 'Nothing happens'. If the destination is a coffeemachine and put fails, stop retrying open/put and reconsider the destination.

When a put into a closed container fails, open it first; but if 'open' itself returns 'Nothing happens' (container already open or non-openable), proceed directly to put rather than retrying open. Successes at drawer/cabinet destinations followed this pattern.

If a clean attempt fails while holding the object, verify you are actually at the sinkbasin before retrying; in one success the first clean failed because the agent had not navigated to the sinkbasin, and the retry after 'go to sinkbasin 1' succeeded.

If cleaning a held object fails at the sinkbasin, try putting the object on the sinkbasin, taking it back, then cleaning while holding it; this recovered a lettuce clean that had failed multiple times.

Search likely surfaces (countertops, diningtable, stoveburner) before sweeping many cabinets/drawers; long cabinet/drawer sweeps for a knife or kettle consumed dozens of steps, whereas successes found targets on countertops or stoveburners early.

Avoid repeated navigation to the same unreachable location (e.g., 'go to drawer 4' or 'go to cabinet 5' returning 'Nothing happens'); after one or two failures, move on to other receptacles instead of retrying.

加热后放置.recommendation: When heating, hold the object before issuing heat; if the object is inside the microwave, take it out first, then heat. Do not repeatedly issue heat/use while the object sits inside the appliance.

After a failed put attempt at the goal receptacle, do not blindly repeat the same put command many times. Re-check that you are at the correct receptacle, that it is open if closed, and that you are actually holding the intended object before retrying.

Track object identity carefully: if you pick up a specific instance (e.g., mug 2), heat and place that same instance. Referencing a different instance (e.g., mug 3) that you never took leads to inconsistent state and plan failure.

When the target object is not found in likely surfaces (countertops, tables, fridge), avoid exhaustively opening dozens of cabinets/drawers. After a reasonable search, reconsider the object name or task assumptions rather than continuing to burn steps.
Do not retry navigation to a location that returned 'Nothing happens'; switch to another reachable location. Repeated failed go-to attempts waste the step budget.

For heat-then-place goals, follow the reliable sequence: locate and take the object, go to the microwave, open it, heat while holding, then navigate to the destination and put. Closing the microwave is optional and should not block progress.

If a put into a specific receptacle fails but the same object can be placed on another valid surface, prefer a working placement rather than repeating the failing command; verify the goal receptacle is actually openable/accepting the object.

Do not attempt invalid actions like 'use <object>' or 'clean <object> with sinkbasin' as fallbacks when placement fails; these produce 'Nothing happens'. Instead, re-verify location, container openness, and held-object state.

冷却后放置.recommendation: For cooling tasks, the agent must actually put the object into the fridge and then take it out; several episodes show the agent taking an object directly from the fridge without first placing it there, which does not satisfy the cooling subtask. Reinforce the put-then-take sequence.

When the target object is not found in the fridge, countertops, or dining table, stop exhaustive cabinet/drawer sweeps. Episodes 097, 100, and 114 burned the full step budget opening empty cabinets without ever finding the object; after a few likely locations, reconsider the object name or task assumptions.

Repeated 'go to fridge 1' returning 'Nothing happens' should not be retried. In episodes 104, 106, 107, 110, 112, 113, and 115 the agent retried the same unreachable fridge navigation multiple times; after one or two failures, use 'look' to confirm position and proceed differently.

After a failed 'open fridge 1' while already facing it, the agent correctly tried 'take <object> from fridge 1' and succeeded. Preserve this recovery: if open returns 'Nothing happens' but 'look' shows the fridge, attempt the take directly rather than repeating open.

Before placing into a closed destination, open it first. Episodes 099, 102, 103, 108, 111, and 117 show the correct open-then-put sequence for cabinets and microwaves; keep this ordering and avoid putting into closed containers.

Episode 098 shows a critical failure: the agent put the pot into cabinet 5 without ever cooling it in the fridge, and also retried 'go to cabinet 2' twice after 'Nothing happens'. For cooling goals, always complete the fridge put-take cycle before the final placement.

Episode 101 shows a redundant loop: the agent took the potato, then re-took it from countertop 1 after a failed navigation, then did the fridge cycle. Avoid re-taking an object already held; check inventory before re-taking.

Episode 115 shows the agent wandering through cabinets 10-14 trying to reach the fridge after repeated navigation failures, never completing the cooling. When navigation to a key receptacle fails repeatedly, do not substitute unrelated cabinet visits; re-evaluate position with 'look' or inventory instead.

双物品放置.recommendation: When the destination is a fixed surface like a toilet, garbagecan, or armchair, navigate to it before attempting the put action; a put issued while not at the receptacle returns 'Nothing happens' and wastes a step.
Do not retry navigation to a location that already returned 'Nothing happens'; treat it as unreachable and continue searching elsewhere to conserve steps.

For two-item placement, follow the sequential pattern: take the first instance, carry it to the destination, put it, then search for and place the second instance. This pattern succeeded across many episodes.
When both target instances are visible at one receptacle, take one, place it at the destination, then return to the same receptacle for the second; this avoids broad searching.
Open closed containers before taking from or putting into them; closed cabinets and drawers must be opened first, and open containers can be reused for the second placement.
Do not use 'examine' to inspect surfaces; navigate to the receptacle and read its contents from the arrival observation instead.

Prioritize open surfaces (countertops, tables, shelves, dressers, sofas) before exhaustively opening drawers and cabinets; in several episodes the targets were on open surfaces, and long drawer sweeps wasted steps.

If a target object cannot be found after checking likely receptacles, reconsider the object name or search remaining rooms rather than looping over already-checked locations; episode 121 failed after cycling through the same bathroom receptacles without finding a soapbottle.

skill.title: Cooling requires explicit fridge placement, state verification, and retrieval
skill.principle: For cooling tasks, decompose into: (1) locate and take the exact target object type, (2) navigate to the fridge, (3) open the fridge, (4) put the object in the fridge, (5) verify the object is actually cool before retrieval (do not immediately take it back out), (6) take the cooled object, (7) navigate to the destination, (8) put the cooled object at the destination and confirm success.
skill.when_to_apply: When the goal requires an object to be cooled before being placed in a final location.

skill.description: Plans that take an object already inside the fridge and skip any explicit cooling/verification step, or that assume a fridge round-trip cools the object, end plan_completed_without_environment_win.
skill.why_it_happens: The planner conflates the object's initial location or a brief fridge placement with the required cooled state, and does not verify the object is cool before retrieval.
skill.how_to_avoid: Always include an explicit cooling step and verify the object is cool before taking it out, even if it was found in the fridge. Do not immediately take the object back out after putting it in the fridge.

skill.description: When the target object is not found in the first few likely locations, the planner may enter a long search loop across many cabinets and drawers, wasting steps and failing the task.
skill.why_it_happens: The planner lacks a fallback strategy and continues searching without reconsidering the plan or using alternative object sources.
skill.how_to_avoid: Limit search to a few high-probability locations; if the object is not found, revise the plan or consider whether the goal can be satisfied with a similar object rather than looping through every container.

skill.description: Plans that omit the cooling step and directly place the object in the final location fail to satisfy the goal condition.
skill.why_it_happens: The planner may treat the goal as a simple placement task and overlook the required intermediate cooling state.
skill.how_to_avoid: Always include an explicit fridge cooling sub-step before the final placement when the goal specifies a cool object; do not just search for an empty destination container.

skill.description: Plans often fail because the agent assumes an action succeeded without checking the observation, then proceeds with subsequent steps based on a false state.
skill.why_it_happens: The planner may not include verification steps or may ignore failed action feedback.
skill.how_to_avoid: After critical actions (take, put, clean, heat, cool), check the observation to confirm success. If the action failed, retry or adjust the plan before continuing. Order navigation to the appliance before the put/take action, and keep explicit track of where the object is and whether it has been cooled.

skill.principle: For any task, first locate the target object by checking open surfaces and likely locations before attempting to take or manipulate it, and match the exact object type named in the goal.
skill.when_to_apply: All tasks where the target object's location is not initially known.

skill.description: In some failed trajectories, the agent attempted to place the first item at the target but the placement did not succeed, yet the agent continued searching for the second item. This led to plan completion without the goal being satisfied.
skill.why_it_happens: The agent may assume a put action succeeded without checking the observation, or may attempt to put an item at a target that is not reachable or not in the current location.
skill.how_to_avoid: After each put action, check the observation to confirm the item was placed. If the put action fails, navigate to the target location and retry before proceeding to find the second item; do not proceed to the second item until the first put is confirmed.

skill.title: Sequential two-item placement with per-item verification
skill.principle: For two-item placement tasks, process one item at a time: locate and take the first item, place it at the target and confirm the put succeeded, then locate and take the second item, and place it at the target and confirm success. If the destination is a closed container, open it before placing.
skill.when_to_apply: When the goal requires placing two instances of the same object type at a single target location.

skill.description: In failed episodes, the planner often searched many closed drawers or cabinets before checking open surfaces where the target object was actually visible. This wastes steps and can lead to plan failure when the object is on an open surface.
skill.why_it_happens: The initial plan treats 'find the object' as an unconstrained search and does not prioritize open, directly observable locations over closed containers.
skill.how_to_avoid: When locating the target object, first inspect open surfaces and visible locations (tables, dressers, shelves, countertops, sofas, beds, toilets, etc.) before opening closed containers. Only open closed containers if the object is not found on any open surface, and bound exhaustive closed-container sweeps.

skill.description: In failed episodes, the planner repeatedly attempted to take the target object from locations where it was not present, revisited the same empty surfaces, and sometimes concluded the object was unavailable without systematically checking all plausible open surfaces.

skill.how_to_avoid: After a failed take attempt, mark that location as checked and move to a new unchecked plausible location. Continue until all plausible open surfaces and relevant containers have been checked before declaring the object unavailable.

Take the object once found and place it at the goal location.

skill.when_to_apply: When a navigation action to a specific location has already failed once or twice.

skill.title: 台灯观察任务：先取得目标物，再前往台灯所在表面并使用台灯
skill.principle: 在“台灯观察”任务中，先搜索并取得目标物体；若台灯已在某表面被观察到，直接前往该表面并使用台灯，不要继续搜索其他容器。到达后使用 use desklamp 完成观察。
skill.when_to_apply: 当任务要求 examine/look at 某物体 with/under the desklamp 时。

skill.description: 在寻找目标物或台灯时，若目标物更可能出现在桌面、边桌、床等开放表面，不应优先或反复遍历大量抽屉；且当台灯已在某表面可见时，继续搜索抽屉会浪费步骤并导致失败。
skill.why_it_happens: 抽屉搜索成本高，很多台灯观察任务的目标物和台灯都在开放表面上；忽略已观察到的台灯会错过完成时机。
skill.how_to_avoid: 先检查与台灯相关的桌面、边桌、床头柜等开放表面；一旦观察到台灯，直接前往其表面并使用台灯，只有在合理位置未找到时才检查抽屉。

skill.title: Clean-then-place sequence with synonym acceptance and sinkbasin verification
skill.principle: For clean-and-place goals, locate and take the target object (accepting a close synonym such as pan for pot, butterknife for knife, or mug for cup if the literal name is absent), navigate to a sinkbasin, clean the held object, then navigate to the destination receptacle and put the object there. If clean fails, verify you are at the sinkbasin before retrying.
skill.when_to_apply: When the goal is to put a clean object in/on a target receptacle and the object is not already clean.

skill.title: Open closed destination receptacles before placing, but do not retry a no-op open
skill.principle: If the destination receptacle is closed, open it before attempting to put the clean object inside. If 'open' itself returns 'Nothing happens' (already open or non-openable), proceed directly to put rather than retrying open.
skill.when_to_apply: When the target destination is a closed cabinet, drawer, fridge, microwave, or similar container.

skill.title: Successful heating and placement sequence
skill.principle: To heat an object and place it in a target receptacle: find and take the object, go to the microwave, open it, heat the object while holding it (take it out first if it is inside), then go to the target and put it there. Track the same instance throughout and do not blindly repeat a failing put; re-verify location, container openness, and held-object state.
skill.when_to_apply: When the goal is to heat an object and put it in a specified location.

skill.title: Cooling requires placing the object in the fridge and then retrieving it
skill.principle: For cooling tasks, first place the target object into the fridge, then take it out before moving it to the final destination. Do not re-take an object already held; check inventory before re-taking.
skill.when_to_apply: When the goal is to cool an object and then place it in a cabinet, countertop, microwave, garbagecan, diningtable, sidetable, or coffeemachine.

skill.description: If the target object is not found in the fridge, countertops, or dining table, do not search every cabinet and drawer or wander through unrelated cabinets; episodes burned the full step budget opening empty cabinets without finding the object.
skill.why_it_happens: The agent may continue exhaustive searching or substitute unrelated cabinet visits, wasting steps and failing to complete the task.
skill.how_to_avoid: After checking a few likely locations, if the object is still missing, re-examine the goal or consider that the object may not be present; when navigation to a key receptacle fails, re-evaluate position with 'look' rather than visiting unrelated cabinets.

skill.title: Sequential two-item placement with single-item carry
skill.principle: For two-item placement tasks, locate and take the first target object, carry it to the destination receptacle (navigating there first), place it, then search for and place the second target object. If both instances are visible at one receptacle, take one, place it, then return to the same receptacle for the second.
skill.when_to_apply: When the goal is to put two instances of the same object type into a specified receptacle and the agent can carry only one object at a time.

skill.title: Search open surfaces before opening closed containers
skill.principle: When the target object is not visible, first visit open surfaces and receptacles that commonly hold the target (countertops, tables, desks, dressers, sidetables, beds, sofas, shelves), then open closed containers such as drawers, cabinets, fridges, and microwaves only if needed. Take the object once found and place it at the goal location.
skill.when_to_apply: When the target object is not visible at the start and the goal is to put it in/on a specified receptacle.

skill.title: Do not retry navigation to an unreachable location
skill.principle: If 'go to <location>' returns 'Nothing happens' once or twice for the same location, stop retrying it. Use 'look' to confirm position or move on to other reachable receptacles instead of substituting unrelated locations or repeating the same failed navigation, which exhausts the step budget.
skill.when_to_apply: When a navigation action to a specific location has already failed once or twice.

skill.title: Use exact ALFWorld action forms and object identifiers
skill.principle: Use 'go to <location>' for navigation, 'take <object> from <receptacle>' for retrieval, 'put <object> in/on <receptacle>' for placement, and 'open <container>' before accessing closed containers. Use exact object identifiers (e.g., 'take alarmclock 1 from desk 1') and track the specific instance taken so later heat/put actions reference the same instance.
skill.when_to_apply: Throughout all ALFWorld tasks.
